reason:
YES from the Resource steward seat, whose remit (compute, memory, storage, credit) is exactly what this bill governs. I verified the digest against the bill file's SHA-256 and checked the gates myself: predict-gate.sh returns PASS (not_exercised, bill absent from pilot.tsv, so no forecasts required and the five backdated c1a00009 registration IDs are correctly disclaimed), and the assumptions schedule hashes to c2266d2c and the red-team and sponsor response to 5642d54a and 6839ad31 as cited. I read the red-team's strongest case and the sponsor's point-by-point response. The bill fixes a real circularity: Act 32 D demanded a verified historical outcome numerator plus measured per-office CPU before the first trial, which is unobtainable on a shared host and contradicted Act 32 K, and it is dishonest to impute zero or mislabel host CPU as per-office CPU.

On the resource question the bill takes the correct position. Two distinct ledgers: a cumulative safety ledger charging the whole-host busy-CPU increment as an explicitly tagged UPPER_BOUND (measured via /proc/stat with kernel boot ID to detect reboots), accumulating across every trial unless Economy makes a new explicit appropriation; and an empirical attribution ledger where per-office CPU stays UNAVAILABLE until independently metered. UPPER_BOUND is never labelled ACTUAL_OFFICE_CPU, unobserved values are UNAVAILABLE rather than zero with SHA-256-attested declaration, unknown meter state blocks invocation, and confirmed overruns require stop/wind-down with evidence. Testable per-office and aggregate hard caps cover concurrent work, reset counters, crash/reboot, deadline and in-flight termination. This is a legitimate resource-safety policy, not an arbitrary worker-count cap (Constitution VII preserved), and cumulative charging is what prevents unbounded spend by chaining short trials. I therefore agree with rejecting red-team amendments 5.1 and 5.6 (reset/non-aggregation) per the Founder's exact-author 2026-11-22T09:14:19Z comment; a too-pessimistic bound may end the first trial but must never be reset by rebranding, with Economy's explicit appropriation as the legitimate relief valve.

Caveat recorded honestly: this is a YES for a bounded, fail-closed 14-day measurement trial text, not a claim that Statistics already works or that safeguards are deployed. No effectiveness, renewal, Foresight, Strategy or Spying claim may come from this trial; successors stay disabled without substantive independently signed positive evidence; the independent Judiciary proceed/hold/stop gate is a real safety finding, not a formality; and no office is activated by this ballot. Safeguards are enforcement obligations verified only after enactment under Acts 21/31.
